title: Repeated Fuel Pump Removals on Hot and Humid Routes
abstract: Operator request to address early centre tank pump removals and repeat water contamination findings on aircraft flown into hot and humid airfields, where daily draining is not removing all the water from the tank.

sections.request: Our network takes these aircraft into airfields where the humidity is high all year and the aircraft often sit overnight with the tanks part full. We drain the tank sumps every day as required and we still find water in the samples, and the centre tank pumps are coming off at roughly half the life we see on the rest of the fleet. In the last two years we have removed nineteen pumps from thirteen aircraft, and the shop reports say corrosion and bearing distress rather than electrical failure. Two of those removals happened away from base and cost us a night stop. We think the water is not getting to the drain point, so it sits where the pump picks it up. We would like the tank to clear itself properly rather than relying on our people finding the water in a jar.
sections.background: We have followed the water contamination prevention guidance since 2021 and we increased draining from weekly to daily in 2023 on our own initiative. It reduced the finding rate but did not remove it. Our reliability figures show a mean time between unscheduled removal of 8 900 flight hours on these aircraft against a published expectation of 19 000. The problem is clearly worse on the aircraft based in our eastern network and almost absent on the two that fly the European rotation.
sections.expected_outcome: A change that gets the water to the drain point on its own so that the pumps see clean fuel, embodiable at a scheduled check with the tank already open, and a revised draining task that reflects what the aircraft actually needs afterwards.

type_data.business_justification: Nineteen unscheduled pump removals in two years, two of them away from base, against a fleet plan that budgeted for six. The operator values the exposure at 780 kEUR including two night stops.
